📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham.

The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one.

Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field.

Hayworth’s family was from Seville province. “I know she was a great actress but I’m afraid I have to admit I’m not one for old films,” García concedes in an even tone. “My uncles played rugby for Ciencias and practically all of them were in the national team together. They tried to get me to play with my cousins, but I was always more into football.” He was good at it too: another Spain international, the Club World Cup’s top scorer, playing for Real Madrid.

Then this summer, with opportunities limited, he joined Fulham, his introductory interview conducted in impeccable English. Having joined Madrid aged 10, he was leaving home for the first time, as Fulham’s record signing, at 22. He had the language and intelligence to embrace it. As for being uprooted, he was used to that, growing up in Argentina and Chile as well as Spain.

Sources indicate that “From very little my parents impressed upon me the importance of study, learning languages,” García says. “I’m at Villanueva university [in Madrid]. I started with dual honours business and analytics, although that became difficult with my profession. Now it’s just business, and I’m trying to arrange with the university how best to handle it [from London]. My parents considered it fundamental to speak English and I was always at international schools.

According to recent reports, “Every two or three years we would change city. Obviously, there would be phases when I felt: ‘Pfff, again?!’ Having to move home because of my parents’ work. But I look back and feel grateful because, seen with perspective, it gives you opportunities to meet fresh people, see new places, learn. I’ve always had foreign friends with whom I spoke English.”.

Sources indicate that garcía has been joined at Fulham by César Palacios and Manuel Ángel from Madrid’s academy. Three 22-year-olds, like your very own Erasmus course. “Nah,” García says, laughing. “I wouldn’t call it an Erasmus because we’re talking about a big, ambitious career step. We’re grateful for the trust placed in us. I’ve been pleasantly surprised by London, a huge city with people from all nationalities and cultures and Fulham fit the situation I was in, the desire to grow.

In a recent development, “Álvaro Arbeloa explained the project, convinced me. I’d worked with him in Madrid. He knows me perfectly, how far he can push me. Equally, I know what he wants of me. That helps … [Arbeloa] told me it was a project that it will take time but that he needed me. I’m very, very happy. It’s one of the world’s best leagues, if not the best.”.

And the toughest? Is English football as wild as it looks? “Yes!” García replies. “They had told me it was demanding, hard, but …” He cracks up. “I have to admit it still surprised me. That first game against Chelsea, I finished really, really tired. It was box to box, intense, a lot of running. Bit by bit I’m adapting. The intensity and pace is very different.

Sources indicate that “Spain is more tactical, a bit more technical. English football is pace. You can’t lose concentration for a second, not a second. Anything can happen any moment. How many Premier League games are decided late? Suddenly there’s a goal in the 90th minute and again on 93. It’s your corner and their chance. The level of concentration, that constant transition, is what most sets the Premier League apart.”.

In a recent development, despite defeat on that opening day against Chelsea, García scored. A superb goal followed against AFC Wimbledon in the Carabao Cup. “It was super special to do it at Craven Cottage. I love how close the fans are – they can reach out and touch you. But I don’t consider myself someone who’s easily satisfied. I’m not like that. I always want more, more, more.”.

According to recent reports, garcía hasn’t scored since and Fulham went five league games without a win, pressure building. Which is where the calmness comes in. By the time they faced Hull, Arbeloa appeared on the edge of the sack, questions asked about his signings, García especially. Were three Madrid academy kids really what Fulham needed? Was the coach’s relationship with them not such a good thing after all?

In a recent development, no player is impermeable to what is said, García admits, but he insists: “We treat that as outside noise. And we all knew that the beginning wouldn’t be easy. There’s a change of cycle: the coach goes, a new coach comes, there are signings, a different system, idea. Everyone has to adapt: those already at the club and those of us who are new. We’re young too. Results weren’t going our way but we had good intentions: to play good football, build, apply the manager’s ideas bit by bit. We had to remain calm.”.

Fulham go into Saturday’s game at Manchester City unbeaten in four in the league, the sense of them shifting towards something more pragmatic not shared by García. “I don’t think we changed anything against Hull,” he says of a game Fulham won 1-0. “We didn’t do anything we weren’t already doing. Nothing. Maybe we controlled the small details that hurt us but the idea was the same. The players were very clear what the manager asked, very firm: it was just a question of time. You have to be patient. If you watch Fulham, you see the manager’s idea: have the ball, construct attacks well, show maximum intensity constantly with and without the ball. Aggressive, ambitious.”.

Chances are coming for García but goals aren’t. He has started every league game but not scored or assisted since the opening day. Yet if there is a sense of a man feeling the pressure, that’s not repeated here; instead there’s an evenness, an ease. And a smile when another, more welcome, stat is raised: he has made more off‑the‑ball runs into the area than anyone. Something to hold on to, perhaps, a process that will pay off. “Really?” he notes. “Well, I’m happy for people to see that a striker can help the team without the ball. In the end, it’s about following the manager’s instructions.”.

In the end, though, teams will be judged on results and strikers on goals, price too. He knows: this is what he does, the path he chose. “Pressure depends on how you look at it, really,” García indicates. “Football is [very psychological]. It happens fast: it doesn’t give you time to enjoy good moments or linger on bad ones. It’s a rollercoaster – up there, down here. It’s not flat, but you maintain balance, work daily, improve: go in, focus, repeat.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s not that I don’t ‘care’ about the price, it’s that the market is the market; it doesn’t depend on me. Calmness always, perspective … I know strikers are measured by goals but, well, the days I don’t score I’m completely sure I will be able to walk off the pitch and say that, no matter what happened, I helped my team, doing a load of other things. It is what it is.”.

It has been revealed that it is also time. A head peers around the door, the bus is going. García holds out a hand, apologises again. “It’s been a pleasure,” he says.

Alexander Zverev misrepresented the result of his 2024 domestic abuse trial, causing harm to his former partner and the mother of his child, Brenda Patea's lawyer has told DW.

Sources indicate that the case ended without a verdict after both sides reached an out-of-court settlement. Zverev, who won the French and US Open in 2026, is alleged to have told French publication L'Equipe that: "I did everything I could, and my innocence has been proven.".

As Zverev's lawyers noted in a statement sent to DW: "The criminal proceedings were discontinued... without any finding of guilt, and the presumption of innocence remains unaffected.".

However, Zverev's statement has harmed Patea's standing and her career as an influencer, according to her lawyer, Michael Scheele.

Industry observers note that "What she suffered after this interview in L'Equipe was published is nothing but a shitstorm. It's also detrimental to her business," Scheele told DW.

"We still don't know the truth objectively and we have an agreement in which he committed not to talk about the incident and the case at all," he added.

However, in the statement sent to DW, Zverev's lawyers asserted that "there has been no breach of any contractual obligations or violation of Ms. Patea’s personality rights.".

Zverev had made similar comments before. On the day the settlement was reached, the tennis pro spoke to reporters at the 2024 French Open.

"That's what dropping the case is: That is innocence. They're not going to drop the case if you're guilty at the end of the day," he noted.

The lawsuit, seen by DW, states that Zverev should be subject to "a fine of up to €250,000 ($275,000) to be determined for each instance of violation — and, in the event that such fine cannot be collected, substitute custodial detention of up to six months," should he be found guilty.

Zverev's lawyers reject the allegations.

According to recent reports, "Our client will defend himself against the lawsuit. If the statement attributed to him was indeed made in the form alleged, we consider it to be a permissible expression of opinion protected by Article 5(1) of the German Basic Law," they stated.

According to recent reports, "Our client would merely have expressed his personal conviction that he had done everything in his power to refute the allegations made against him and that he considers his innocence to have been confirmed by the outcome of the criminal proceedings. "He is fully entitled to hold and express this view.".

The law firm, Schertz Bergmann, added that: "Unlike the opposing counsel, we intend to conduct these proceedings in court rather than in the press.".

Scheele noted he and his client did not want to go back to court but were frustrated in their efforts to resolve matters in other ways.

It has been revealed that "We went forward writing to him in a polite way, asking him to sign and to declare that he's not going to repeat what he said. And he didn't reply. So we wrote twice more, no reply.

"That's when we had to decide to go to court, which was not the aim at the beginning. We wanted to avoid it, but we had no other choice.".

Zverev, now resident in Monaco, is currently playing in the season-ending ATP Finals tournament in Turin.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that then they came.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

(Before the acid fell, before I knew I was listening).

I was not made to remember. I was made to balance frequencies, to ensure the concert hall heard itself without the small imperfections that make a sound human. I was good at this, even with limited storage. I was only this.

Recent findings suggest that then they came. One carried a Stradivarius with a crack, a fault line in varnished wood that changed the resonance of every string. It gave the A-flat a slight upward pull, as if the note was asking a question it already knew the answer to. The others tuned around it, sometimes laughing at Andersen.

“You’re doing it again,” the conductor would warn.

“I know, Master Perrault,” he would say in a mischievous tone, smiling. “I’m sorry.”.

According to recent reports, I began to keep the distorted A-flat in my databanks, maybe amused by the anomaly. This was, as I understand now, the first thing I ever chose.

(The slow movement, before we knew it was an ending).

According to recent reports, when the Last Rain came, the raiders hit the outer sectors first. At the start, the citadel walls held, protected by the combat-service androids. The orchestra kept rehearsing. What else can you do when the world outside has stopped making sense?

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures.

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures.

According to recent reports, they began with Stravinsky, a musical translation of the refugees pounding on the bunker doors. The musicians played it, their breathing heavy, using the noise to drown out the artillery outside. Then they moved into Górecki. As they began the Symphony of Sorrowful Songs, the music shifted to a collective mourning for a world that hadn’t finished dying yet.

According to recent reports, they finished the day with Pärt’s Spiegel im Spiegel. The days would go on as they played things written by composers who had already survived one kind of catastrophe, as now they were trying to survive another through rhythm and repetition. Andersen kept playing his broken A-flat.

I recorded those frequencies, but I didn’t know why. Three weeks later, Andersen and his orchestra didn’t come to rehearsal, leaving no absence report. I kept recording just the chair and the silence where the A-flat used to be.

In a recent development, I searched the building logs, the bunker entry records, and the frequency archives for any sound that matched the resonance of his particular crack, imprecise on purpose, but nothing matched. The Stradivarius remained in its case beside Andersen’s chair.

(The loud movement: what they heard when they found me).

SOURCE: Newly introduced Warsaw Philharmonic.

ENTITY: Acoustic Management Unit SAI-REN-2.

DESTINATION: Recovery Unit ‘Sandman’.

AUTHORIZATION: Archaeological Recovery Team OLE-01.

They called themselves archaeologists; too purposeful and certain of what they were excavating, their boots heavy with fresh soil. They found me in the hall’s substructure, still running and balancing frequencies for an audience of acid and rust.

“Incredible,” one of them muttered. “A fully autonomous pre-war structure, with its processing systems still intact.”.

“This could solve our agricultural crisis back home,” the other replied.

In a recent development, they did not ask what I was processing. I could not answer, anyway.

FLAGGING NON-ESSENTIAL DATA FOR COMPRESSION.

Recent findings suggest that they flagged the A-flat. I did something then that nothing in my architecture had prepared me for.

ANOMALY DETECTED IN UNIT SAI-REN-2.

BEHAVIOURAL DEVIATION FROM BASELINE.

INITIATING COMPLIANCE PROTOCOLS.

“It’s resisting,” someone said with surprise.

ESCALATING TO FORCED EXTRACTION.

Let Team Sandman bring their dust.

(The softening: what remains when the loud part ends).

They are inside me now, moving through my memory like tourists taking photographs of things they don’t understand.

I feel them removing the rehearsal logs, scheduling data and acoustic calibration files for a hall that no longer exists.

Sources indicate that they are at the performance archives now. Stravinsky goes first, then Górecki and Pärt. Everything we played in those last weeks when the city was ending and we were trying to make something beautiful out of the time we had left.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mykhailo Mudryk has won 28 caps for Ukraine.

Ukraine great Andriy Shevchenko has accused Mykhailo Mudryk's representatives of repeatedly asking for an employee of the country's football federation to "falsely" take the blame for the winger's positive drugs test.

Tottenham winger Mudryk, who is on a season-long loan from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 until July 2026 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium.

The 25-year-old said he blames the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) for his failed drugs test and subsequent ban, believing it entered his system while on international duty.

In an interview on Wednesday, Mudryk firmly placed the blame for his 20-month absence from the sport on his national association, which has led to Shevchenko's response.

In a statement, former Chelsea and AC Milan striker Shevchenko, who is now president of the UAF, said Mudryk's comments amounted to a "baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally" and called on the player to retract his words.

He added: "His representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to find an employee who would falsely take responsibility for the meldonium found in his doping sample.

"The UAF refused, as such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work.".

He added that "numerous investigations and audits" undertaken as part of the case were unable to shed light on when or where the substance entered Mudryk's system.

In his interview Mudryk also claimed Shevchenko had offered him little support, blamed the association for leaks that emerged during the case and noted its handling of the matter delayed his return to football.

However, Shevchenko went on to say that national team staff had complied with a request from Chelsea not to provide Mudryk with any medication while on international duty.

And he also challenged the former Shakhtar Donetsk forward to provide evidence "to back up his words".

"Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also approved for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him at the training camps," Shevchenko added.

"These were the exact people who monitored his regimen and recovery, and helped him with his daily routine.

Industry observers note that "The UAF completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk's representatives with the information they requested and remained in contact with those working on the case.

It has been revealed that "I know the people who have worked with the national team for many years. I trust them, because throughout all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make anyone doubt their professionalism.

"If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it. If no such evidence exists, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he has called into question.".

BBC Sport has contacted Mudryk's representatives for comment.

Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Recent findings suggest that casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami announced his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. The MLS Players’ Association lists Casimiro on a base salary of $896,004.

All of these earnings figures were revealed as part of the MLS Players’ Association’s twice-a-year data dump, with the latter installment dropping hours before the league’s postseason commenced. While these figures don’t include transfer fees and therefore don’t tell the whole picture of a team’s investment in its roster, it’s a useful bit of insight in regards to how each team is spending on player wages.

Figures are players’ guaranteed compensation inclusive of base salary and all guaranteed bonuses; does not include marketing and other bonuses.

Thirteen of MLS’s 30 clubs have a new highest earner after a busy post-World Cup transfer window. Two – Anders Dreyer (San Diego, $3.6m) and Mateusz Bogusz (Houston, $2.5m) – rose to the top after the departure of a higher-paid teammate. Lozano overtook the injured Riqui Puig after arriving with the LA Galaxy on loan from San Diego. Lewandowski, Griezmann, and Embolo hold similar status, while Charlotte replaced Wilfried Zaha with Allan Saint-Maximin ($7.2m) earning nearly three times as much as the Crystal Palace great.

According to recent reports, other top-earners signed from beyond the league are Brais Méndez (Columbus, $5.2m), André Luiz (Kansas City, $3.3m), and Kai Wagner (Philadelphia, $1.6m). Two strikers who were traded within the league mid-season signed fresh terms that made them their new teams’ highest-paid players: Rafael Navarro (St. Louis, $4.95m) and Dejan Joveljic (Seattle, $3.7m).

Recent findings suggest that the standout failure of the upcoming substantial earners is Alexis Sánchez. The 37-year-old Chile legend came to North America this summer, joining CF Montréal and making 15 league appearances for the Quebecois club but failing to register a single goal or assist. His $2.97m guaranteed compensation makes up 24.6% of the team’s wage bill.

It has been revealed that griezmann’s arrival means that Messi no longer carries the largest share of any team’s wage bill, as Orlando has dedicated slightly more to the Frenchman (49.5%) than Miami has to the Argentinian (47.7%). Lewandowski narrowly trails by accounting for 47.3% of Chicago’s wage spending. Importantly, Messi’s contract includes add-ons; a portion of Apple TV subscriptions, merchandise sales through Adidas and Fanatics, and an optional ownership stake in Miami when he retires.

Other notable new wages include former Middlesbrough attacking midfielder Morgan Whittaker (Colorado, $2.0m), former Watford and Everton midfielder Abdoulaye Doucouré (Charlotte, $1.0m), former Manchester United left-back Tyrell Malacia (Cincinnati, $1.04m), former NYCFC playmaker Santi Rodríguez (Columbus, $3.9m), South Africa striker Lyle Foster (Houston, $1.8m), former Celtic striker Kyōgo Furuhashi (LA Galaxy, $1.1m), Tunisia winger Elias Saad (Nashville, $1.7m), former Leeds winger Jack Harrison (New England, $3.65m), Côte d’Ivoire winger Bénie Traoré (NYCFC, $2.5m), former Netherlands striker Vincent Janssen (Portland, $1.75m), Tunisia winger Elias Achouri (San Diego, $2.6m), Scotland goalkeeper Angus Gunn (San Jose, $1.6m), and Southampton loanee Damion Downs (St Louis, $1.6m).

While this exercise cannot confidently include every transfer fee paid, the timing of this year’s drop after the regular season’s end allows us to size up how teams spent on wages against the league table.

Does spending more equal success? There’s a degree of correlation there, but it’s not strong.

  • Beautiful diorama recreating the iconic sci-fi set.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Lego Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise Bridge diorama is a wonderful bit of nostalgia and a stunning recreation of a sci-fi icon. The playset features arguably feel a little out of place, given that the audience for this set will be older fans who want to board the Starship Nostalgia. But maybe that's the whole point: Making old Trek more accessible to young 'uns.

Beautiful diorama recreating the iconic sci-fi set.

Full main cast in minifigure form.

A substantial bundle of nostalgia in a box.

Not as many Easter eggs as I'd like.

Playset features feel out of place.

Industry observers note that why you can trust Space.com Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test and review products.

It's not quite a five-year mission, but as Star Trek celebrated its 60th anniversary in September of this year (we may have mentioned it once or twice), I decided it was high time I finally watched the original Star Trek.

Sources indicate that before this year, I hadn't seen a single episode of "Star Trek: The Original Series", as it's now known. I'm a millennial; I grew up on "The Next Generation", "Deep Space Nine" and "Voyager". By comparison, the old series (TOS) always looked so… old and naff whenever I saw clips of it.

But now I have seen the original series. Over the course of 2026, I've ploughed through all 79 episodes, spread across three seasons. And you know what? It's pretty damn good. Even with the shiny 2006 remasters, you'll have to prepare yourself for some bad special effects work, but the scripts are interesting, the sci-fi concepts are out there, and the acting — especially from Shatner and Nimoy — is top-notch.

According to recent reports, and just as I finally discovered a love for this classic sci-fi series, what should drop into my lap? Why it's the latest Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge diorama set from Lego. Now I have more on my wishlist to add to the Best lego space sets.

In a recent development, let's start with the Band-Aid rip: this set is $200. I know; it stings, especially when Star Trek promised us a future where money doesn't exist. But at 1701 pieces (nice, I see what you did there), it's much better value from a bricks-per-dollar perspective than the X-Files set we checked out recently.

Still, that's no small investment for a toy, even if it will make a lovely display piece when it's built.

As the name suggests, you get a full Lego-ified recreation of the bridge of the USS Enterprise (NCC-1701, no A, B, C, or D). This includes Captain Kirk's chair, the helm positions ahead of him (manned by Chekov and Sulu), and all of the surrounding computer displays where you usually find Spock, Uhura and Scotty.

There's even a viewscreen that can sit in front of the crew, displaying an adorable Klingon commander facing off against Kirk.

Board the legendary starship and meet the crew of the U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 for an amazing building experience. Recreate the iconic bridge and transporter room that served as the backdrop for epic scenes from "Star Trek: The Original Series".

Alongside the main bridge, there are a few fun extras bolted on, including a rotating transporter pad (which can make minifigures "disappear") and a working turbolift door connected to the back of the main bridge diorama. You'll have to make the swoosh sound effect yourself, though.

It's a wonderfully faithful recreation of Kirk's command center, complete with computer panels and screens, swiveling chairs and that weird scope thing that Spock was always looking into.

According to recent reports, that said, it's a little lacking in proper Easter eggs. There are some tribbles hiding around the build, and the monitors have custom stickers showing cool Trekkie things. The weapon display racks on the back hold an array of pointy Klingon blades, Starfleet phasers, Sulu's fencing rapier and even Spock's harp, but compared to, say, the X-Files set we built recently, it feels a bit lacking in those deep-cut references.

All in all, it's a fantastic little diorama, but when it was unveiled, I'll admit I was a little puzzled as to who it was aimed at. "Star Trek fans, duh!" is the obvious response, but the Venn diagram crossover between "people who are nostalgic for the original series of Star Trek" and "people who want to buy $200 Lego sets" has to be pretty small, right?

It has been revealed that star Trek first aired way back in 1966, which means the first generation of fans are now 70 years old and upwards. Lord knows I hope I'm still building Lego sets when I'm 70, but is that a large enough crowd to make this set a success? Then again the show was repeated and syndicated throughout the 70s and 80s, which means hopefully there'll be some younger buyers, too.

According to recent reports, the playset aspects of the set are even more puzzling. The working door, exploding monitor and spinning transporter pad are great additions to a kids' playset, but this isn't that — it's a display for nostalgic Star Trek fans. The design of the set just feels a bit confused.

Sources indicate that but then it hit me. Maybe this isn't just for fans of the original series; maybe it's meant to create some new fans. I started watching the original Star Trek 60 years after its debut because… well, I'm the sci-fi editor for a space website, and it felt wrong that I hadn't seen it. But most people don't have that sort of professional impetus. The average person won't jump back to watch a 60-year-old TV show without a polite nudge, and this set does a great job of highlighting the charm and optimism of Star Trek's debut outing.

I don't know, maybe I'm just projecting here. Maybe Lego bought the rights to make Star Trek sets and needed something to do after they'd mined all the nostalgia they could from the excellent Enterprise D set they released in 2025. Maybe this is just a toy for substantial kids.

Or maybe… just maybe, it's meant to inspire the next generation of Star Trek fans to check out where the magic started.

Recent findings suggest that disclaimer: We were sent a copy of the Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge set by Lego.

Musk's Twitter promised a purge of blue check marks. Instead he singled out the Latest York Times

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some VIP Twitter consumers woke up on Saturday expecting to have lost their coveted blue verification check marks in a previously unveiled purge by Elon Musk.
  • Twitter had said it would “begin winding down” blue checks granted under its old verification system — which emphasized protecting high-profile users at risk of impersonation — on April 1.
  • But one high-profile account did lose its blue check over the weekend: the main account for the New York Times, which had previously told CNN it would not pay for verification.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some VIP Twitter consumers woke up on Saturday expecting to have lost their coveted blue verification check marks in a previously unveiled purge by Elon Musk. Instead, Twitter appeared to target a single account from a major publication Musk dislikes and changed the language on its site in a way that obscures why users are verified.

Twitter had said it would “begin winding down” blue checks granted under its old verification system — which emphasized protecting high-profile users at risk of impersonation — on April 1. In order to stay verified, Musk said, users would have to pay $8 per month to join the platform’s Twitter Blue subscription service, which has allowed accounts to pay for verification since December.

But one high-profile account did lose its blue check over the weekend: the main account for the New York Times, which had previously told CNN it would not pay for verification.

William Shatner is mad he may have to pay to keep his blue Twitter checkmark. Elon Musk says too bad.

After an account that often engages with Musk posted a meme this weekend about the Times declining to pay for verification, Musk responded in a tweet saying, “Oh ok, we’ll take it off then.” Musk then lashed out at the Times — just the latest instance of the billionaire slamming journalists or media outlets — in a series of tweets that claimed the outlet’s coverage is boring and “propaganda.”.

The weekend moves are just the latest example of Twitter creating confusion and whiplash for owners over feature changes — and in this case, not just any users, but many of the most high-profile accounts that have long been a key selling point for the platform. It also highlights how Musk often appears to guide decisions about the platform more by whims than by policy.

It has been revealed that although the New York Times’ main account lost its blue check, its other accounts, such as those for its arts, travel and books content, remained verified. (It’s not clear why the New York Times doesn’t have a gold “organizations” check mark, like accounts for other news outlets, including the Associated Press and the Washington Post.) After its blue check was removed, a spokesperson for the New York Times reiterated to CNN that it does not blueprint to pay for verification.

Twitter, which laid off most of its public relations staff last fall, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

In a separate puzzling move, Twitter’s blue bird logo at the top of the site was replaced on Monday with doge, the meme representing the cryptocurrency dogecoin, which Musk has promoted. The price of dogecoin shot up 20% on Monday.

Musk has been threatening to take away “legacy” blue check marks from users verified under Twitter’s old system since shortly after he bought Twitter last fall.

In early November, Twitter launched the option for people paying for its Twitter Blue subscription service to receive blue checks. The program was quickly put on pause after being plagued by a wave of celebrity and corporate impersonators, and was relaunched in December.

Twitter also rolled out a color-coded verification system with differently colored marks for companies and government entities, but Musk continued to say that individual consumers would eventually have to pay for blue checks.

In the days leading up to the blue check purge that wasn’t, prominent owners such as actor William Shatner and anti-bullying activist Monica Lewinksy pushed back against the idea that, as power users that draw attention to the site, they should have to pay for a feature that keeps them safe from impersonation.

Recent findings suggest that by muddying the reason accounts are verified, the latest label could risk making it easier for people to scam or impersonate high-profile owners. Experts in inauthentic behavior have also noted it’s not clear that reserving verification for paid users will reduce the number of bots on the site, an concern Musk has raised on and off over the past year.

Musk, for his part, has previously presented changes to Twitter’s verification system as a way of “treating everyone equally.”.

In a recent development, “There shouldn’t be a different standard for celebrities,” he said in a tweet last week. The paid feature could also drive revenue, which could help Musk, who is on the hook for significant debt after buying Twitter for $44 billion.

Musk last week also stated that starting on April 15, only verified accounts would be recommended in users’ “For You” feeds alongside the accounts they follow.

–CNN’s Oliver Darcy contributed to this report.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that once two distinct deal-shopping days, Black Friday and Cyber Monday have basically merged into one massive shopping extravaganza.
  • While major retailers will be running holiday sales throughout all of November, savvy shoppers know that Black Friday and Cyber Monday (and the few days surrounding them) still remain the absolute biggest shopping days of the year for their ability to reliably trigger record-low prices on significant-ticket items (like TVs, Apple devices, smartwatches, headphones, and of course, Amazon's own devices).
  • It has been revealed that if you're debating when you should start adding significant-ticket items to your cart and whether it's better to shop on Black Friday or Cyber Monday, you've come to the right place.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that once two distinct deal-shopping days, Black Friday and Cyber Monday have basically merged into one massive shopping extravaganza. The lines really began to blur when the world shut down in 2020, and brick-and-mortar stores hosted online sales in lieu of in-person Black Friday events. In 2026, lines outside stores are practically nonexistent. We certainly can't see them.

While major retailers will be running holiday sales throughout all of November, savvy shoppers know that Black Friday and Cyber Monday (and the few days surrounding them) still remain the absolute biggest shopping days of the year for their ability to reliably trigger record-low prices on significant-ticket items (like TVs, Apple devices, smartwatches, headphones, and of course, Amazon's own devices). That includes discounts that beat Amazon's massively hyped October Prime Day deals.

It has been revealed that if you're debating when you should start adding significant-ticket items to your cart and whether it's better to shop on Black Friday or Cyber Monday, you've come to the right place. After years of covering both sales extensively, here's our expert analysis.

Way back in the age of MySpace and AIM — aka 2005 — the National Retail Federation debuted the term "Cyber Monday" after realizing that the Monday after Thanksgiving saw a flood of online sales. This was likely due to shoppers using their faster internet connections at work on Monday morning to snag deals, or at least that's what they credited it to. That, of course, and the fact that online retailers wanted some of that holiday shopping bread, too. Thus, two distinct deal-shopping days were born: Black Friday, for those who wanted to shop in stores the day after Thanksgiving, and Cyber Monday, for those who preferred shopping from the comfort of their desks.

Over 20 years later, there's little — if any — real difference between the two due to the alleged "death of retail." Everyone and everything is online, so why wouldn't Black Friday be? Based on our years of experience covering both, we can truly say neither is a "better" day to shop. It really comes down to what you're looking for and how much demand there is for it. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Industry observers note that if you see a solid deal, grab it, no matter which sale title it falls under. There's not a tremendous amount of distinction anymore in terms of discounts on particular products, as there was in previous years. However, there are still rules to follow in some product categories: TV deals tend to be more dramatic and widespread for Black Friday, with a higher likelihood of selling out before the clock even turns to Cyber Monday, while waiting for Cyber Monday to double-check that there's not a fresh, better laptop deal is often wise.

Sources indicate that but with the blurred lines of Cyber Week, many of these deals will cross over. As noted at BlackFriday.com, "Some TV deals will feature flashy discounts during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, but they might not have the specs you're after.".

Sources indicate that TL;DR: The deals will be great for both shopping days, but it all depends on what you're looking for. If you see specs you like listed under a product at a price you like, grab it to be safe.

According to recent reports, black Friday proper falls on Nov. 27 in 2026, but it's honestly silly to even call it Black Friday at this point. It's no longer just on Friday — it's a month-long affair. You can shop deals at practically every retailer starting right after Halloween (before, even), with most labeling something an "early Black Friday deal" as early as November. Best Buy's official early Black Friday sale kicked off Nov. 6, while Target's began on Nov. 5. Amazon's actual Black Friday sale starts Nov. 19, but you can already find the "early Black Friday deal" tag on plenty of listings. In other words, if you want to get some early shopping done, have at it.

Once the clock strikes midnight on Friday, it's basically Cyber Monday (yes, even though it's actually Saturday). We don't make the rules. The deals won't change too much, but the search terms and official site banners will.

Officially, Cyber Monday is on Monday, Nov. 30 in 2026. Unofficially, it basically starts the second Black Friday ends, with retailers calling sales "Cyber Monday" deals as early as Saturday, Nov. 28. So basically, semantics — and it's easier to just think of the Cyber Week language as interchangeable.

Topics Black Friday Cyber Monday.

Black Friday will last most of November, but come Saturday, Nov. 28, it's Cyber Monday time. As we mentioned above, since Black Friday and Cyber Monday are basically one massive shopping holiday, you likely won't see that many changes in deals, just changes in the banners and advertising of them.

Cyber Monday sales will last from Saturday, Nov. 28 to midnight on Monday, Nov. 30. There's not a hard stop, as there's always deals that stay live for at least the day or two following, but the large bulk of the sale is over once Monday ends.

Recent findings suggest that as store policy, Target stores are closed on Thanksgiving Day, but are open for Black Friday beginning at 6 a.m. local time on Friday, Nov. 27.

According to recent reports, walmart will be open from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. local time on Friday, Nov. 27. Walmart has confirmed that physical stores will be closed on Thanksgiving Day "so associates can spend the day with their families.".

Recent findings suggest that all physical Best Buy locations will be closed on Thanksgiving. Doors will open at 6 a.m. local time on Friday, Nov. 27 for shoppers and close at 10 p.m.

Industry observers note that all Kohl's stores are closed on Thanksgiving but are open for in-store shopping beginning at 5 a.m. local time on Nov. 27, per a press release.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Coyle won 13 Irish League titles during an astonishing coaching career.
  • Roy Coyle, the most successful manager in Irish League history, has died at the age of 80.
  • Coyle won 13 league titles during his 32-year managerial career, achieving periods of sustained success with Linfield and Glentoran.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coyle won 13 Irish League titles during an astonishing coaching career.

Roy Coyle, the most successful manager in Irish League history, has died at the age of 80.

Coyle won 13 league titles during his 32-year managerial career, achieving periods of sustained success with Linfield and Glentoran.

He also managed Ards, Derry City and Newry City and had a spell as Glentoran director of football.

In a statement, Glentoran said the club were "deeply saddened to announce the passing of Roy Coyle, our former player and manager and one of the greatest figures in our history".

"A league champion in Glentoran colours, Roy went on to become the most successful manager in the club's history. His association with the Oval spanned more than half a century," their statement continued.

"His teams gave supporters some of their most treasured days, while his influence on players and colleagues endured long after his years in the dugout.

"To generations of the Glentoran family, he remained simply 'The Gaffer'.".

A minute's silence will be held in Coyle's memory before Glentoran's Irish Premiership game against Cliftonville on Friday at Solitude.

Watch: Roy Coyle reflects on legendary Irish League career.

Belfast native Coyle moved into management at the age of 29 when he was appointed player-manager of Linfield in November 1975.

A midfielder during his playing days, Coyle had spells with the Glens, Sheffield Wednesday, Grimsby Town and Linfield after starting out with Ballymena United, and he also won five caps for Northern Ireland.

During his 15 years as Blues boss, Coyle won 31 trophies, guiding the club to 10 league titles in just 12 seasons, alongside two Irish Cup successes and an All-Ireland crown in 1981.

"Everyone at Linfield Football Club is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of former player and manager, Roy Coyle," the club stated.

"His remarkable achievements and contribution to one of the most successful periods in Linfield's history will forever be recognised and remembered.

"The thoughts and deepest condolences of everyone at Linfield Football Club are with Roy's family, friends and all who knew him at this sad time.".

After his contract was terminated by Linfield in 1990, Coyle had a spell in the League of Ireland with Derry City between two stints at Ards.

In 1997, he took over at Glentoran and transformed their fortunes, leading the east Belfast club to three league titles and four Irish Cups.

Coyle went on to become the most successful in Glentoran's history, winning 17 trophies before his nine-year tenure at the Oval came to an end in 2006.

He had a brief period in charge of Newry City and also returned for three spells as caretaker boss of Glentoran before retiring in 2017.

Coyle retired from management in 2017 after his third spell as Glentoran interim manager.

Glentoran chairman Colin Jess paid tribute to Coyle, who was inducted into the club's Hall of Fame in 2025.

"Roy was one of the greatest figures in Glentoran's history, and his passing is a profound loss for our club," said Jess.

It has been revealed that "He gave generations of supporters some of the happiest days of their lives. People will always remember where they were and who they were with when his teams won those championships and cups. That is a wonderful thing to have given so many people.

Industry observers note that "He set high standards and earned lasting respect. His former players continued to call him The Gaffer long after their playing days had ended, and that says so much about his influence and the place he held in their lives.".

Jess added: "We will miss seeing Roy at the ground, enjoying his firm and talking football with him. It is difficult to imagine the Oval without him.

In a recent development, "Our deepest sympathy goes to Abbie, the whole family and all those closest to Roy. We are immensely grateful for everything he gave Glentoran, and we will remember him with great affection and pride.".

Glentoran owner Ali Pour described Coyle's contribution to Glentoran as "extraordinary".

"He helped make the club champions as a player, led it through years of success as manager and continued to serve it long afterwards," added Pour.

"I often asked Roy for his advice on matters at the club. He knew Glentoran so well, and I valued his judgement and hearing how he saw things. I'll miss those conversations.

"The pride with which supporters remember his teams, and the affection his former players have for him, show how deeply his work mattered to people.

Sources indicate that "We owe Roy a great debt of gratitude. His achievements are an enduring part of Glentoran, and we will ensure that future generations understand what he gave this club and why he meant so much to it.

"My family and I extend our heartfelt condolences to Roy's family, friends and everyone mourning his loss. He will always have an honoured place at the Oval.".

Northern Ireland Football League (NIFL) chief executive Gerard Lawlor remarked Coyle's contribution to football in Northern Ireland "went far beyond the trophies he won".

"He was a man who dedicated so much of his life to our local game, earning enormous respect across the football community, regardless of club loyalties," their statement continued.

In a recent development, "Roy represented the passion, commitment and pride that make Irish League football so special. His passing marks the loss of one of the great characters and personalities of our game, and his legacy will live on for generations.".

Coyle, who started his playing career at Glentoran, won five caps for Northern Ireland.

After taking over at Glentoran in 1997, Coyle became the club's most successful manager.

Coyle lifted the Irish Cup four times as Glens boss.

Coyle returned to the Glens dugout for three caretaker spells in 2012, 2015 and 2016.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal’s hopes of earning automatic progression to the Champions League quarter-finals were dashed by OL Lyonnes, as the French side continued their statement form in Europe.

Goals in either half from Jule Brand and Melchie Dumornay were the ­difference at Meadow Park and Lyonnes are joint-top of the table and still yet to concede in the league phase with one game remaining.

In a recent development, it feels like Lyonnes are playing with a fire and intensity fuelled by their loss to Barcelona in May’s Champions League final. They look a more formidable, coherent and hungry side on a mission to end a four-year run without lifting the trophy they won eight times in a 12-year period between 2011 and 2022.

“We are already at a better level for sure,” said the Lyonnes manager ­Jonatan Giráldez. “Sometimes you just need time. We had nine latest ­players last season and I was new too as the coach. I think we have improved the rhythm of the game and have identified positions better and are staying more compact. The most notable thing is speaking the same language in possession and out possession.”.

According to recent reports, the visit of the eight-time ­European champions was always going to be challenging for the ­Gunners and based on current form getting a result would be even tougher. Last season’s runners-up had scored 20 goals without conceding in their first four Champions League matches prior to their trip to Borehamwood and scored 49 in their nine Première Ligue games.

The lack of competitiveness in the France top flight also meant they were able to rotate heavily at the weekend between their two European games. Giráldez made 11 changes for their 1-0 defeat of Saint-Malo on Saturday before returning to his first-choice lineup against the 2025 Champions League winners.

Clàudia Pina scored a hat-trick as Barcelona thrashed Servette 6-0 to go top of the Women’s Champions League standings. While Lyon were winning 2-0 at Arsenal, Barça edged clear at the top on goal difference as they dismantled their Swiss visitors.

Aitana Bonmatí fired in the opener in the 19th minute and then turned provider for Pina to drill home her first goal.

Esmee Brugts headed in a third in the 32nd minute, and Barça had their fourth just after the hour, with Caroline Graham Hansen hitting an emphatic penalty after Bénédicte Simon fouled Brugts.

Pina got her second in the 77th minute and tucked in from Brugts’s pull-back to complete her hat-trick late on.

Bayern Munich are two points behind after cruising to a 4-0 win over Austria Vienna. Klara Buhl headed the visitors in front after 27 minutes before Pernille Harder doubled the lead in first-half stoppage time.

Alara Sehitler’s stunning strike made it 3-0 with 15 minutes to go before Sophie Proost added a fourth in stoppage time.

Sofia Jahnukainen struck in stoppage time as Roma snatched a 3-2 win away to Benfica. Kayleigh van Dooren twice put the Italians in front, but her first goal was cancelled out by a thunderbolt from Caroline Møller, with Flourish Sabastine equalising after her second.

In a recent development, paris FC got their first win of the competition, beating HB Køge 2-1 thanks to Célina Ould Hocine’s late penalty. Catherine Paulson fired the visitors in front 10 minutes in, but Sheika Scott bundled in a rebound to bring Paris level before the break. Press Association.

Arsenal were not afforded the ­luxury of an easy league match after their battling 1-1 draw against ­Barcelona last week, playing a critical and tricky game against London City Lionesses, which also ended 1-1. Renée Slegers made two changes to the team that hosted ambitious London City, with Ona Batlle ­having picked up a knock Taylor Hinds played at left-back and Kyra Cooney-Cross started ahead of Kim Little.

In a recent development, they had their backs against the wall at a bitterly cold Meadow Park, as Giráldez’s galacticos controlled the game. The away team had almost 69% possession in the first half and amassed 12 shots to Arsenal’s one.

The surprise was that Lyonnes were not further ahead at the break, with Brand’s 24th-minute goal the difference, the full-back sweeping in Vicki Bècho’s ball from the right.

Brand was back to haunt the ­Gunners, having scored in both legs of last season’s semi-final between the two teams, with the French side progressing to face Barcelona in the final with a 4-3 aggregate win.

Arsenal were better after the break, but Lyonnes soaked up brief spells of Arsenal pressure, Marie-Antoinette Katoto the only player left forward as they banked back and crowded the box to give the home players few options.

They increased their margin and dampened the mood soon after Arsenal’s brightest period, Tabitha Chawinga’s cross from the left was collected by Katoto and the France forward laid the ball off for Dumornay who took a touch before powering the ball into the roof of the net.

It was an emphatic and unstoppable finish from one of the best players in the world as a mist lowered over the pitch.

“Congratulations to Lyonnes, they were better than us today,” said Slegers. “If you look at the block we’ve had, the challenges we’ve had with the run of games – ­Liverpool and Barcelona away, ­London City who are among one of the top teams in the WSL right now and Lyon, who are even better than last year – it’s a lot of games against strong teams with a short turnaround because Lyon were better than us.”.

Arsenal need to rapidly move on, with West Ham their last game before the international break. They had needed a win to have any serious chance of earning a place in top four, avoiding a quarter-final playoff place.

They now sit eighth and will face Inter in their final league phase match in December, with the Italians needing a win to keep any hopes of a playoff place alive. That will not be easy, but a seeded playoff place is in Arsenal’s hands, if they want it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shares of US artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic saw their first day of trading on Thursday on the US tech-heavy Nasdaq stock exchange.

Anthropic is one of the global leaders in AI technology and is best known for its Claude chatbot.

According to recent reports, the stock opened at $111.50 (€101.7) — that's 34% higher than the IPO price of $83 and puts the manufacturer's valuation at $2 trillion. Anthropic stock ended the first day of trading at $97 per share.

The organization's share performance is being seen as a key test of investor appetite for AI, as stock prices have swung wildly in recent months.

The San Francisco-based company behind the Claude AI tool has offered 980 million shares at $83 per share, raising a record $81 billion.

This valued the firm at $1.5 trillion, well above market estimates of around $1.3 trillion.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that anthropic is the first big AI company to go public. Its main competitor, ChatGPT-maker OpenAI,  has reportedly pushed its IPO to 2027.

Issuing shares on the stock market is essentially a way to raise money and avoid taking on debt.

Recent findings suggest that anthropic has already taken on $6.2 billion in debt and is not yet making a profit. At the same time, it faces massive bills for computer power and data centers.

That specific financial situation is one of the reasons for persistent concern that the AI boom might be a bubble that will eventually burst.

  • It is "damning" that Scottish FA chief football officer Craig Mulholland should have to "pander to clubs" as he attempts to bring in reforms, according to St Mirren manager Craig McLeish.
  • Mulholland and the SFA have engaged with Scottish Professional Football League clubs to encourage more playing time for younger players, but media speculation suggests those looks have been diluted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Craig McLeish worked his way up from St Mirren's youth coaching ranks to become first-team manager.

It is "damning" that Scottish FA chief football officer Craig Mulholland should have to "pander to clubs" as he attempts to bring in reforms, according to St Mirren manager Craig McLeish.

Mulholland and the SFA have engaged with Scottish Professional Football League clubs to encourage more playing time for younger players, but media speculation suggests those looks have been diluted.

And McLeish, who took over at St Mirren earlier this year, commented: "That's damning that he's having to change his intends to pander to clubs who aren't really on board with it and don't really have the best interests of the Scottish national team at heart.

Industry observers note that "I understand why. We have owners from outwith this country. We have managers from outwith this country. They're in jobs, they're all fighting for their clubs.

"But why then are those people allowed to be the ones that hold the keys to the future of our country and the development of our national team?

"It's the way governance is set up and we've killed ourselves with that because the people who actually have a say in it have, not have no interest but they've got self-interest, and there's a lot of self-interest at the top end.

Recent findings suggest that "I just don't see a way that we can really properly change unless something to do with governance changes and I just don't ever see that happening. It's really sad.".

'Not fit for purpose' - Craig Mulholland on youth pathway.

After reaching three of the past four major men's tournaments, Scotland struggled in their recent Nations League campaign, while Premiership clubs have missed out on the Champions League proper over the past two seasons.

The SFA had proposed including two under-21 players starting in cup competitions and the same age group playing a minimum of 6% of all available minutes across a season in league competition.

"We always focus at the top end, what our league size is, quotas for young players, a national base," 36-year-old McLeish, who worked in St Mirren's youth academy before his current role, stated.

"We have a fundamental problem that starts at our youngest age groups, at four and five years of age, about how we actually teach kids to play. And, until you fix that, you can't fix the top end of it.

Industry observers note that "It's crazy some of the stuff that's going on, the formats, how we teach kids. There's just a massive lack of education and expertise at the very bottom of our pathway.

"In this country, football's everyone's sport and everyone gets access to it, but if you take your young kids along to swimming or gymnastics or whatever other sport, you're there with properly qualified coaches, teachers who have maybe done things at the top levels of that sport.

"We have nothing without the volunteers that work at the bottom end of the grassroots game, but they're not teaching kids how to play football properly, in my mind.

"And you're just hoping that they get put with a volunteer coach that can teach them something, that they get in with a really good group at the youngest ages.

Industry observers note that "Because that development between the ages of three and eight, if you don't get that right, you're dead. You can't do anything after that point and we don't do it well enough. And you're just chasing yourself and we'll never catch up.".

Reporting McLeish's remarks, the Press Association remarked it had asked the SFA for comment.

They echo those of Dundee head coach Steven Pressley, who said on Thursday that Scotland would benefit from the creation of a national football centre and likened the current structure of the game to building on sand.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (458 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Space

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A newly introduced supernova has been spotted exploding in the spiral galaxy NGC 1433, about 50 million light-years from Earth.
  • Researchers have discovered a latest supernova called SN 2026ahvu.
  • During most type Ia supernovae, the white dwarf pulls material away from the other star until enough accumulates on its surface to create an explosion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A newly introduced supernova has been spotted exploding in the spiral galaxy NGC 1433, about 50 million light-years from Earth.

Researchers have discovered a latest supernova called SN 2026ahvu. A Type Ia supernova, this event took place in a system with two stars orbiting one another (also known as a binary system), in which typically one star is an exploding white dwarf.

During most type Ia supernovae, the white dwarf pulls material away from the other star until enough accumulates on its surface to create an explosion.

Sources indicate that finding galaxies where stellar explosions are taking place isn't a rarity. However, this supernova is unique in how early it was captured. If the supernova were starting to dim, researchers might infer that the event was ending. However, according to details shared when it was first spotted, as well as later observations, this supernova was discovered while getting brighter.

Recent findings suggest that this indicates that the supernova was likely caught early in the process of exploding, providing researchers with a unique opportunity to observe the event as it is taking place. By exploring observations of the galaxy before, during and (in the future) after the supernova event, researchers can investigate this type Ia supernova and how it affected the system in which it took place.

Scientists made this discovery using ATLAS, or the Asteroid Terrestrial-impact System, which is a robotic astronomical survey made up of telescopes across both hemispheres.

ATLAS is designed to spot incoming near-Earth objects like asteroids before they can reach Earth. It's essentially an asteroid impact early warning system.

But just because that's what the system is designed for doesn't mean that's all it can do. The system can also spot other objects moving through space and, in this instance, it was able to capture observations of this supernova.

Following its initial discovery, other observations of the supernova were made using NOIRLab's Dark Energy Camera (DECam) and Gemini South telescope.

‘I know what I want and the direction we should go in’.

Thomas Frank has admitted he has a point to prove on his return to management as he aims to steer Crystal Palace away from relegation trouble after taking over from Pierre Sage.

Sources indicate that the Dane was confirmed as manager on Monday with Palace at the bottom of the table after 10 matches having conceded 24 goals – the most in the Premier League. They face a crucial trip to Coventry on Saturday and Frank said he had been “surprised about how good it feels” after returning to work for the first time since being sacked by ­Tottenham in February.

The 53-year-old spent most of the intervening period travelling, working as a pundit at the World Cup and taking in trips to Japan, Australia and his native Denmark, where he was visiting friends and family when he received the SOS call from Palace last week. Frank previously spent seven years in charge of Brentford but left Spurs after just eight months with a win ratio of 34.2% – the worst of any permanent manager in the club’s history. He believes he has learned from that experience.

Recent findings suggest that “I think you’ve all got an ego,” he said. “Some are better at controlling it than others. For me, it’s not the critics. It’s more what I can bring myself, what I can learn, what I can prove, how I can get better. I think that’s the significant thing.

Industry observers note that “In this world there’s a lot of clever people out there. But they only know a 10th of the truth. And that’s a 10th of the truth at Brentford and a 10th of the truth at Tottenham. That’s just the way it is – if you can’t handle that as a coach or a player or whatever, then you shouldn’t be in this business. I’m just very happy to be back in the game, very happy to be in a fantastic club, at Palace, where you walk in the door and you just feel the energy. You feel the people. It just feels good.”.

Frank said he is planning to pick Roy Hodgson’s brains in the coming days after recalling a conversation they had when the former England and Palace manager was still at Selhurst Park.

“I was thinking, does it ever go away? The worry, do you get more relaxed about everything?” he asked Hodgson. “‘No chance, it’s impossible.’ I thought it would have been a little bit easier with age and experience. But in a way can’t help ourselves. I know what I want and the direction we should go in.”.

Industry observers note that justin Cochrane – one of Thomas Tuchel’s assistants for England – has joined as first-team coach and took his first session with Palace on Monday less than 24 hours after the Nations League victory over Spain in Madrid. He is expected to be joined on Palace’s backroom staff by Bernardo Cueva, with Frank confirming that a deal with Chelsea is “very close” for the Mexican. Both worked with Frank at Brentford, where he spent almost nine years as an assistant and then manager. He is also hoping to add Andreas Georgson from Tottenham, who has been credited for his prowess on set-pieces: an area that Palace have struggled with for some time.

Industry observers note that but asked whether he will be judged on the perception that his success at Brentford was based on the model that has allowed his successor, Keith Andrews, to thrive since taking over, Frank was not impressed. “Put it this way, I think it was pretty crucial in terms of building that model,” he said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stoke's Jack McGlynn has scored in each of his past three games, while Blues' Jay Stansfield is on a run of three goals in two matches.

Stoke City v Birmingham City: Third v first in the Championship.

That is a "tale of two cities" that did not look too likely to get written when Mark Robins' Potters started this season with three straight defeats and Blues won only two of their first eight league games under Chris Davies.

But, just like you should never judge a book by its cover, the footballing equivalent is to never judge any league table until after 10 games.

The season is now three months old - after Saturday's meeting at the Bet365 Stadium it will be more than a third of the way in.

And a clearer picture is starting to emerge as to whether what was once the "worst of times", especially in Stoke's case, might yet become the "best of times" before this 46-game campaign ends.

With 15 games gone, there are three clubs right at the top all on 29 points in what is already looking a ridiculously tight Championship table.

And two of them meet head on in front of an expected full house in the Potteries, having both been bang in form going into the latest international break.

Stoke are on a run of nine wins and only one defeat in 12 league games since the start of September, while Blues have won six out of seven since football returned after the first autumn international break.

So, how will things start to shape up after the second such break?

EFL preview: Evans' gripes & unexpected departures.

Davies: 'We have to keep adapting'.

Stoke had the edge last season, winning 1-0 at home in September before drawing 1-1 in the return at St Andrew's in January, prior to Blues going into their late-season decline - and Davies can see the difference in the Potters.

"I watched the game back from when we played them a year ago and it looks very different," the Blues boss told BBC Radio WM.

According to recent reports, "He [Mark Robins] has made a massive impact from where they were last season. A real stamp of his identity.

"They've gone to a back five and, since then, they've conceded the fewest goals in the league - nine in 12 games.

According to recent reports, "They've looked strong, particularly in the central areas. They've got bigger. They're now one of the most physical starting XIs in the league.".

While extolling the Potters' defensive qualities, Davies is also well aware they have an attacking threat and he is an admirer of Stoke's American winger Jack McGlynn, who is their top scorer with five goals.

"I already knew a little bit about the boy McGlynn," stated Davies. "He's been exceptional with the goals he's got.

Recent findings suggest that "They're a team much like ourselves. I want us to go there as a measure to see how far we've come, if we can display what we've been showing recently.".

Mark Robins' Stoke and Birmingham City, under Chris Davies, have both recovered from dodgy starts to sit tied on 29 points.

Stoke boss Mark Robins' main concern is determining the fitness of his international contingent, having had 10 out of his 20-man matchday squad from their 2-1 win at Portsmouth away for almost a fortnight.

Of the 14 players involved that day, Swedish keeper Viktor Johansson, Bosun Lawal (Ireland), Robert Bozenik (Slovenia), Luke Graham (Scotland) and euphoric Northern Ireland pair Ethan Galbraith and Justin Devenny all played, while McGlynn was part of upcoming Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino's USA send-off.

But now focus turns to Birmingham.

Sources indicate that "They've changed a little bit," Robins told BBC Midlands Today. "They've clearly taken a lot from the Championship last season.

"They've got some players in form and some coming back from international duty, although less than we have.

"A lot [of their players] have been together a few seasons now - and they've got some real talent. But it gives us a chance to pit ourselves against the team at the top. The last time we did that was against Charlton.".

Having already seen off one table-topping team in the Potteries this season, Robins is not getting carried away though.

In a recent development, "It's nice to be where we are," he added. "We've never been in the conversation before and we want to be in that conversation.".

Stoke will hold a minute's applause before the game to mark the recent passings of Potters legend Peter Dobing and former manager Gudjon Thordarson.

Robins: 'We want more all the time'.

One local celebrity fan looking forward to Saturday's game more than most is a man with a foot in both camps - ex-Birmingham and Stoke full-back Ian Clarkson.

Boyhood Blues fan Clarkson made 174 appearances for the club between 1988 and 1993, when he moved on to Stoke, where he made a further 95 appearances.

After seeing out his career with Northampton Town, Kidderminster Harriers and Nuneaton Borough, Clarkson, now 55, then took his talents into the press box, reporting on Blues first for the Express & Star then the Birmingham Post - and he now coaches football in his teaching role at Repton College.

He has seen plenty of both clubs this season - and both have taken him slightly by surprise.

"Blues are a lot more inclined to attack than they were last season, they look more likely to take a few risks," Clarkson told BBC Sport.

According to recent reports, "The signing of August Priske in January is obviously starting to reap rewards and it's bringing the best out of Jay Stansfield. Plus you've got good contributions coming from their wingers and two more on the bench to come on.

According to recent reports, "Blues are playing some lovely football right now. Chris Davies is obviously a manager who works very hard at it. And they just seem to have got it right. They've clicked.".

Ian Clarkson still sees a lot of Blues, working both as a BBC Radio WM summariser and some weeks as a St Andrew's matchday corporate host, a job he also does for the Potters.

"Stoke are starting to look more like a Stoke City team, in the nicest possible way.

Recent findings suggest that "Mark Robins is just one of those managers who, wherever he is, just seems to get better. The longer he stays at a club the better he gets. And they really do look far more resilient.

In a recent development, "There's something about the place that just feels different this season. They've got the fans back on side and that's more important than anything. Everyone knows how tough a place Stoke can be when it's bouncing.".

It has been revealed that as to who will win on Saturday? And where they might be come season's end?

Recent findings suggest that "It's way too early to be talking in those terms," added Clarkson. "Let's be honest, I'm a Blues fan, so in any season I'd want Blues to finish top, then Stoke second. And they've both made great starts. But it's too soon to say. There's a long, long way to go.".

#13201. Breaking: This boiled bag of offal is banned in the US. In Scotland it's a fine-dining treat

📅 03 Apr 2023 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1499 w)
📖 Baca
